evidence: resolveAppInfoByPath: adapter throw -> {ok:false,failed}; adapter null -> existence probe on Contents/Info.plist, which is the exact discriminator darwin.getAppInfoUnstable itself uses (darwin.ts:193-201 ENOENT branch), so 'mdls broke while the manifest is there' -> failed and 'bundle vanished' -> not-app. processAppPath keeps them distinct at the call site too: invalid/not-app (silent, terminal, clears tracking) vs error/scan-failed (logged with the error message, enters the ladder). Non-.app paths cannot reach the probe on macOS because resolveAppPath rejects them first.

domain 'app-index' / operation 'resolve-path' / code / userImpact 'degraded' matches the two existing app-index reports (process-path:3105, manual-rebuild:4027); context goes through sanitizeContext like every other caller.

backoff is scheduled, never awaited inline: handleAppResolutionFailure only arms a setTimeout and processAppPath returns immediately, so handleIndexedSourceWatchEvent releases the per-source mutation lease at once. Ladder 2/8/30s then dead letter (40s worst case, matches the diagnosis). Overflow past APP_RESOLUTION_RETRY_MAX_TRACKED_PATHS=64 dead-letters immediately instead of growing; dead letter itself capped at 64 with oldest-eviction. Sweep interval created only when the set becomes non-empty and cleared on drain (both in sweepAppResolutionDeadLetters and in forgetAppResolutionFailure). All timers unref'd. Teardown: prepareForSearchIndexShutdown -> clearAppResolutionTimers (app-provider.ts:686); search-core.ts:2109 -> router.unsubscribe -> both queues dispose.

Last-writer-wins is real and load-bearing: removing `coalesce: ({next}) => next` from the router makes 'resolves an in-place bundle replacement to the add rather than the delete' fail with 'expected delete to be add' (the SDK default returns the delete). App key truncates at the first '.app/', so /Foo.app/Contents/Frameworks/Bar.app groups onto /Foo.app, agreeing with resolveAppPath's own indexOf('.app') truncation. hasPendingWindow/dispose lifecycle covered on both sides (one timer while open, zero when closed, zero while idle, dispose keeps pending entries).

probeFilesystem:true appears at exactly two decision points -- _ensureStartupIndexHealth (2072) and the dev recent-backfill guard (2243). getIndexedSourceHealth (975), which the UI can poll, stays count-only. No periodic caller.

Zero-threshold set difference means one miscount buys a full backfill every launch, and two inputs could miscount. (1) macOS hands out decomposed names where the stored row is composed -- both sides now go through normalizeFsPath with an explicit 'darwin' platform constant (A3's PATH_NORMALIZATION_PLATFORM precedent; the ambient FS_PLATFORM is captured at module load and the tests redefine process.platform afterwards). (2) a directory merely named *.app can never produce a row, so it pinned the source unhealthy forever -- an entry now has to carry Contents/Info.plist to be counted, at one access per UNMATCHED entry, zero on a healthy index. Empirical baseline on this machine: 104 depth-1 bundles vs 229 app rows, exactly 1 genuine miss (Doubao Browser.app, one of the three chunk-load casualties), no case/NFC divergence.

Relaxing `healthy: unindexedOnDisk === 0` to `<= 3` turns both F4 assertions red (health.healthy stays true; appRuntimeScan('startup') never fires), so the single-app sensitivity is guarded, not incidental.

publishAppRuntimeUpsert('app-resolution-retry-upsert') builds its record through mapScannedAppToIndexedSourceRecord, the same mapper the watch route uses at app-provider.ts:1163, so keywords/extensions projection is identical; only action ('change' vs the event's) and reason differ, matching the existing 'app-manual-path-upsert' precedent.

A later watch event could put a parked path back on the ladder while it was still in the dead letter; if the sweep's processAppPath then won the processingPaths race, the retry run returned reason 'processing' and, because the sweep runs with scheduleRetry:false, nothing re-armed -- the retry entry leaked one of the 64 slots permanently. The sweep now skips any path the ladder still owns. Test 'leaves a parked path to the ladder when a later event puts it back on one' goes red without the guard (6 resolutions instead of 5).

moveAppResolutionToDeadLetter is reached both by an exhausted ladder and by retry-slot exhaustion; the latter logged 'exhausted 0 retries' and reported context.attempts=0. It now carries an explicit cause ('retries-exhausted' | 'retry-slots-full') into both the log line and the report context.

app-provider.realtime-freshness.test.ts spent the cold Vite transform of the provider's module graph inside whichever test ran first (3.7s warm, >5s cold -> timeout). A beforeAll warm-up now absorbs it: first test 3661ms -> 334ms, file 8.06s -> 5.56s on a cold cache.

afterEach now restores fs spies (clearAllMocks only drops recorded calls, the stubbed implementation survived into later tests); the F6 dev-gate test restores NODE_ENV instead of deleting it, since vitest sets it for the whole worker.

detail: An mv-based in-place upgrade has a window where Contents/Info.plist is absent; a resolve landing exactly there classifies as not-app and gets no retry. The 400ms coalescing window makes the resolve fire after the last event of the burst, so the window is small, and the subsequent add events re-trigger. Noted, not fixed.

residual: reason token reaches the toast raw
detail: addAppByPath now answers reason 'scan-failed' where it used to answer 'not-app'; SettingFileIndexAppIndexManager.vue:196 does toast.error(result.reason || <i18n fallback>). Pre-existing for every reason token ('invalid-path', 'processing', ...), so this is not a new gap, but the token set grew. Belongs to a broader i18n pass, not here.

The classified resolveAppInfoByPath replaced every call site. The nullable wrapper is kept deliberately -- the AppScanner test doubles still expose getAppInfoByPath and ~10 existing app-provider tests assert against that mock, so deleting the real method would leave the double describing a method that no longer exists. The test name and comment now say that instead of claiming 'existing callers'.

residual: app queue holds every file path for its window
detail: The app queue receives all FILE_ADDED/CHANGED events, not just bundles, so a large burst (a clone into a watched root) transiently holds one Map entry per unique path in both queues for up to 400ms. Total routing work is unchanged -- previously the same events were fired as unawaited promises into the same serial gate -- and the burst bounds the memory, so no action taken.
